subject: Mathematics
questionText: A hollow closed cube of side 10 cm, each weighing 200 gm, is made. This cube is placed in water with a horizontal face. How many cm of its height sinks in water if the density of water is 1 gm per cm³?
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
According to the Law of Flotation, Weight of a floating object = Weight of displaced liquid.

Base Area × Submerged Height × Density of liquid = Weight of object
⇒ (10 × 10) × h × 1 = 200
⇒ 100 × h = 200 ⇒ h = 2 cm
∴ The correct answer is 2 cm.

Alternate Method
Given:
Side of the closed cube (a) = 10 cm
Weight of the cube (W) = 200 gm
Density of water (ρ) = 1 gm/cm³ Formula Used: Volume of a cuboid = Base Area × Height
Weight = Volume × Density
Law of Flotation: A floating body displaces its own weight of the fluid in which it floats.

Calculations:
⇒ Base area of the cube = Side × Side = 10 × 10 = 100 cm² ⇒ Let the height of the cube that sinks in water be h cm.
⇒ Volume of water displaced = Base area × Submerged height = 100 × h = 100h cm³ ⇒ Weight of displaced water = Volume of displaced water × Density of water
⇒ Weight of displaced water = 100h × 1 = 100h gm

According to Archimedes' Principle:

⇒ Weight of the cube = Weight of the displaced water
⇒ 200 = 100h
⇒ h = 200 ÷ 100 = 2 cm
∴ The correct answer is 2 cm.

Additional Information
Archimedes' Principle

Any object wholly or partially immersed in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object.

Law of Flotation

An object will float if its average density is less than the density of the fluid. In equilibrium, the floating object displaces a weight of fluid strictly equal to its own weight.

Density and Volume Relation

Density (ρ) is defined as mass (or weight in a uniform gravitational field) per unit volume. Calculated as Weight = Volume × Density.

subject: Mathematics
questionText: A field roller, in the shape of a cylinder, has a diameter of 1 m and length of 1 1/4 m (i.e. 5/4 m). If the speed at which the roller rolls is 14 revolutions per minute, then the maximum area (in m²) that rolls in 1 hour is:
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Area rolled in 1 revolution = Curved Surface Area = πdh
Area per revolution = 22/7 × 1 × 5/4 = 55/14 m² Total revolutions in 1 hour (60 min) = 14 × 60 = 840
Total area = Total revolutions × Area per revolution
Total area = 840 × (55/14) = 60 × 55 = 3300 m² ∴ The correct answer is 3300 m².

Alternate Method
Given:
Diameter of the roller (d) = 1 m
Length of the roller (h) = 1 1/4 m = 5/4 m
Speed = 14 revolutions per minute
Time = 1 hour = 60 minutes

Formula Used:
Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cylinder = π × d × h
Total Area Rolled = Total Revolutions × CSA

Calculations:
⇒ Total revolutions in 1 hour = 14 revolutions/minute × 60 minutes = 840 revolutions
⇒ Area covered in 1 revolution (CSA) = (22/7) × 1 × (5/4)
⇒ Area covered in 1 revolution = 110/28 = 55/14 m² ⇒ Total area rolled in 1 hour = 840 × (55/14)
⇒ Total area = (840 ÷ 14) × 55
⇒ Total area = 60 × 55
⇒ Total area = 3300 m² ∴ The correct answer is 3300 m².

Additional Information
Cylinder Properties

Volume = πr²h | Total Surface Area = 2πr(r + h) | Curved Surface Area = 2πrh or πdh

Revolutions and Rolled Area

When a cylindrical roller rolls on the ground, the flat area covered in one full revolution is exactly equal to its Curved Surface Area (CSA).

Revolutions and Linear Distance

If a wheel or roller moves forward, the linear distance covered in one revolution is equal to the circumference of its circular base (2πr or πd).

subject: Mathematics
questionText: If the total surface area of the right circular cylinder is 50% more than the curved surface area of that cylinder and the volume of right circular cylinder is 5488π m³, then find the curved surface of the right circular cylinder. (in m²)
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
TSA is 50% more than CSA ⇒ TSA = 1.5 × CSA
⇒ 2πr(r + h) = 1.5 × 2πrh ⇒ r + h = 1.5h ⇒ h = 2r
Volume = πr²h = πr2(2r) = 2πr³ ⇒ 2πr³ = 5488π ⇒ r³ = 2744 ⇒ r = 14 m
CSA = 2πrh = 2πr(2r) = 4πr² = 4π(14)² = 784π m² ∴ The correct answer is 784π m².

Alternate Method
Given:
Total Surface Area (TSA) = Curved Surface Area (CSA) + 50% of CSA = 1.5 × CSA
Volume (V) = 5488π m³ Formula Used: TSA = 2πr(r + h), CSA = 2πrh, Volume = πr²h

Calculations:
⇒ 2πr(r + h) = 1.5 × 2πrh
⇒ r + h = 1.5h
⇒ r = 0.5h ⇒ h = 2Rs. ubstitute h = 2r into the volume formula:
⇒ πr2(2r) = 5488π
⇒ 2πr³ = 5488π
⇒ r³ = 2744
⇒ r = 14 m
Now find height (h) and CSA:
⇒ h = 2 × 14 = 28 m
⇒ CSA = 2πrh = 2 × π × 14 × 28
⇒ CSA = 784π m² ∴ The correct answer is 784π m².

Additional Information
Right Circular Cylinder Geometry

Total Surface Area (TSA) is the sum of the Curved Surface Area (CSA) and the two circular bases: TSA = 2πr² + 2πrh.

Ratio of Areas

The relationship between TSA and CSA directly gives the ratio of radius to height since TSA ÷ CSA = (r + h) ÷ h = 1 + (r ÷ h).

Volume of Cylinder

The volume represents the total 3D space enclosed within the cylinder, given by the product of the base area and the height: V = πr²h.

subject: Mathematics
questionText: What is the volume of a hemisphere with radius 2.8 cm? (Use \(\pi=\frac{22}{7}\)) (Rounded up to three places of decimal).
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
For a hemisphere, apply the direct formula: Volume = 2/3 × π × r³ Substitute r = 2.8 cm: V = 2/3 × 22/7 × (2.8)³ V = 44/21 × 21.952 = 965.888 ÷ 21
V ≈ 45.9946... cm³ Rounding to three decimal places gives 45.995 cm³.
∴ The correct answer is 45.995 cm³.

Alternate Method
Given:
Radius of the hemisphere (r) = 2.8 cm

Formula Used:
Volume of a hemisphere (V) = 2/3 × π × r³ Calculations:
⇒ V = 2/3 × 22/7 × (2.8)³ ⇒ V = 44/21 × (2.8 × 2.8 × 2.8)
⇒ V = 44/21 × 21.952
⇒ V = 965.888 ÷ 21
⇒ V = 45.99466... cm³ ⇒ Rounding to three decimal places, V = 45.995 cm³ ∴ The correct answer is 45.995 cm³.

Additional Information
Hemisphere Surface Areas

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πr² | Total Surface Area (TSA) = 3πr² Complete Sphere
Volume = 4/3 × πr³ | Surface Area = 4πr² Cylinder
Volume = πr²h | Curved Surface Area = 2πrh | Total Surface Area = 2πr(r + h)

Cone

Volume = 1/3 × πr²h | Curved Surface Area = πrl (where slant height l = √(r² + h²))

subject: Mathematics
questionText: If the total surface area of a hemisphere is 1848 m², then the diameter (in m) of the hemisphere is: (Use \(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\))
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total surface area = 3πr² = 1848
⇒ 3 × (22/7) × r² = 1848
⇒ r² = 1848 × (7/66) = 196
⇒ r = √196 = 14 m
⇒ Diameter (d) = 2r = 2 × 14 = 28 m
∴ The correct answer is 28 m.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total surface area of the hemisphere = 1848 m² Formula Used: Total Surface Area (TSA) = 3πr² Diameter = 2r

Calculations:
⇒ 3 × (22/7) × r² = 1848
⇒ (66/7) × r² = 1848
⇒ r² = 1848 × (7/66)
⇒ r² = 28 × 7
⇒ r² = 196
⇒ r = √196 = 14 m
⇒ Diameter = 2 × 14 = 28 m
∴ The correct answer is 28 m.

Additional Information
Curved Surface Area of Hemisphere

The curved surface area (CSA) includes only the upper dome portion and does not include the circular base. Formula: CSA = 2πr² Volume of Hemisphere

The volume represents the total 3 - dimensional space contained within the hemisphere. Formula: V = (2/3)πr³ Properties of a Full Sphere

For a complete sphere of radius r, the Total Surface Area = 4πr² and its Volume = (4/3)πr³

subject: Mathematics
questionText: For a solid right circular cylinder, its radius and height are in the ratio of 2 : 9 and are melted and recast to a sphere of diameter 24 m. If no metal is wasted during the process, then find the height of the cylinder. (in m)
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Since the cylinder is melted and recast into a sphere, their volumes will be exactly equal.

Let cylinder radius = 2x and height = 9x. Sphere radius = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 m.
⇒ π × (2x)² × 9x = (4/3) × π × 123
⇒ 36x³ = 4 × 576 ⇒ x³ = 64 ⇒ x = 4
⇒ Height of the cylinder = 9 × 4 = 36 m.
∴ The correct answer is 36 m.

Alternate Method
Given:
Ratio of radius to height of the cylinder = 2 : 9
Diameter of the sphere = 24 m ⇒ Radius of sphere (R) = 12 m

Formula Used:
Volume of Cylinder = πr²h
Volume of Sphere = (4/3)πR³ Calculations:
⇒ Let the radius of the cylinder be 2x and the height be 9x.
⇒ Volume of Cylinder = Volume of Sphere
⇒ π × (2x)² × 9x = (4/3) × π × (12)³ ⇒ π × 4x² × 9x = (4/3) × π × 1728
⇒ 36x³ = 4 × 576
⇒ 36x³ = 2304
⇒ x³ = 2304 ÷ 36
⇒ x³ = 64
⇒ x = 4
⇒ Height of the cylinder = 9x = 9 × 4 = 36 m
∴ The correct answer is 36 m.

Additional Information
Principle of Melting and Recasting

When a solid 3D object is melted and reshaped into another, its total enclosed volume remains constant, irrespective of the change in its shape or surface area.

Volume of a Right Circular Cylinder

The volume defines the capacity enclosed by the cylinder walls, evaluated by multiplying the circular base area by its height: V = πr²h.

Volume of a Sphere

A sphere is a perfectly round 3D geometrical shape. The total space occupied is computed with the standard formula: V = (4/3)πR³.

subject: Mathematics
questionText: A hollow sphere of internal and external diameters 4 cm and 8 cm respectively is melted into a cone of base diameter 8 cm. What is the height of the cone?
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
When an object is melted and cast into another shape, their volumes are equal.

Volume of Cone = Volume of Hollow Sphere
(1/3) × π × Rc² × h = (4/3) × π × (R³ - r³)⁴2 × h = 4 × (43 - 23)
16 × h = 4 × (64 - 8) ⇒ 16 × h = 224
h = 224 ÷ 16 = 14 cm
∴ The correct answer is 14 cm.

Alternate Method
Given:
External diameter of the hollow sphere = 8 cm ⇒ External radius (R) = 4 cm
Internal diameter of the hollow sphere = 4 cm ⇒ Internal radius (r) = 2 cm
Base diameter of the cone = 8 cm ⇒ Base radius (Rc) = 4 cm
Let the height of the cone be h cm.

Formula Used:
Volume of a Hollow Sphere = (4/3) × π × (R³ - r³)
Volume of a Cone = (1/3) × π × Rc² × h

Calculations:
Since the shape is completely melted and recast, the volume must remain conserved.

⇒ Volume of the Cone = Volume of the Hollow Sphere
⇒ (1/3) × π × Rc² × h = (4/3) × π × (R³ - r³)

Canceling (π/3) from both sides:

⇒ Rc² × h = 4 × (R³ - r³)

Substituting the given radius values:

⇒ 42 × h = 4 × (43 - 23)
⇒ 16 × h = 4 × (64 - 8)
⇒ 16 × h = 4 × 56
⇒ 16 × h = 224
⇒ h = 224 ÷ 16
⇒ h = 14 cm
∴ The correct answer is 14 cm.

Additional Information
Volume Conserved Concept

Whenever a 3D figure is melted and recast into another 3D figure, the volume remains exactly the same. The sum of the initial volumes equals the sum of the final volumes.

Volume of a Solid Sphere

For a fully solid sphere of radius R, the formula is Volume = (4/3) × π × R³.

Surface Areas of a Cone

Curved Surface Area = π × r × l and Total Surface Area = π × r × (r + l), where l is the slant height and l = √(r² + h²).

subject: Mathematics
questionText: An ice-cream cone with a lid has a total surface area equal to the area of another circle of certain radius. If the radius of the circle is equal to average of the slant height and the radius of the cone, then the ratio of the slant height of the cone to the radius of the circle is:
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total surface area of cone = Area of circle ⇒ πr(l + r) = πR² ⇒ R² = r(l + r)
Given R = (l + r) ÷ 2 ⇒ l + r = 2Rs. ubstitute (l + r) in first equation: R² = r(2R) ⇒ R = 2r
Now, l + r = 2R = 2(2r) = 4r ⇒ l = 3r
Ratio of slant height to circle radius = l : R = 3r : 2r = 3 : 2
∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total Surface Area of an ice - cream cone with a lid = Area of a circle with radius R.
Radius of the circle (R) = Average of the slant height (l) and radius (r) of the cone.
Formulas Used: Total Surface Area of a Cone = πrl + πr² = πr(l + r)
Area of a Circle = πR² Calculations:
⇒ According to the given condition, Area of Circle = Total Surface Area of Cone
⇒ πR² = πr(l + r)
⇒ R² = r(l + r) ............. (Equation 1)
⇒ It is also given that R is the average of l and r:
⇒ R = (l + r) ÷ 2
⇒ Squaring both sides, R² = (l + r)² ÷ 4 ............. (Equation 2)
⇒ Equating Equation 1 and Equation 2:
⇒ (l + r)² ÷ 4 = r(l + r)
⇒ Since l + r is a strictly positive length, dividing both sides by (l + r):
⇒ (l + r) ÷ 4 = r
⇒ l + r = 4r
⇒ l = 3r
⇒ Substituting l = 3r back into the formula for R:
⇒ R = (3r + r) ÷ 2 = 4r ÷ 2 = 2r
⇒ The required ratio of the slant height of the cone (l) to the radius of the circle (R) is:
⇒ l : R = 3r : 2r = 3 : 2
∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.

Additional Information
Total Surface Area of a Cone

It comprises the curved surface area (πrl) and the flat base area (πr²). Therefore, Total Surface Area = πr(l + r).

Volume of a Cone

The volume represents the total internal capacity of the cone. Formula: Volume = (1 ÷ 3)πr²h, where h is the perpendicular height.

Slant Height Relationship

The slant height (l), base radius (r), and perpendicular height (h) form a right - angled triangle. By Pythagoras theorem, l = √(r² + h²).

Area of a Circle

The two - dimensional space enclosed by the boundary of a circle is its area, represented by the formula Area = πR².

subject: Mathematics
questionText: A cylinder of height 28 cm and radius 10 cm is melted and formed into 4 square base pyramids each has the same height H and the base length of each pyramid is equal. Find the height of the pyramid, if the length of its base is 20 cm.
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Volume of Cylinder = 4 × Volume of Square Pyramid
⇒ πr²h = 4 × (1/3 × a² × H)
⇒ 22/7 × 100 × 28 = 4 × 1/3 × 400 × H
⇒ 8800 = (1600/3) × H ⇒ H = (8800 × 3) ÷ 1600 = 16.5 cm
∴ The correct answer is 16.5 cm.

Alternate Method
Given:
Radius of cylinder (r) = 10 cm, Height of cylinder (h) = 28 cm
Base side of square pyramid (a) = 20 cm, Number of pyramids = 4
Let the height of each pyramid be H.

Formula Used:
Volume of Cylinder = πr²h
Volume of a Pyramid = 1/3 × Base Area × Height

Calculations:
When a solid is melted and recast to form new objects, the total volume remains constant.

⇒ Volume of Cylinder = 4 × Volume of Square Pyramid
⇒ πr²h = 4 × (1/3 × a² × H)
⇒ (22/7) × 102 × 28 = 4 × (1/3 × 202 × H)
⇒ (22/7) × 100 × 28 = 4/3 × 400 × H
⇒ 22 × 100 × 4 = (1600/3) × H
⇒ 8800 = (1600/3) × H
⇒ H = (8800 × 3) ÷ 1600
⇒ H = (88 × 3) ÷ 16
⇒ H = (11 × 3) ÷ 2
⇒ H = 33 ÷ 2 = 16.5 cm
∴ The correct answer is 16.5 cm.

Additional Information
Melting and Recasting

When a 3D object is melted and recast into another shape, the total volume always remains constant regardless of the change in dimensions.

Volume of a Cone

V = 1/3 × πr²h, where r is the base radius and h is the vertical height. A cone is essentially a circular base pyramid.

Volume of a Prism

V = Base Area × Height. The volume formula of a cylinder is a special case of a prism with a circular base.

questionText: A hundred rupee note measures 15 cm × 8 cm and a bundle of 125 such notes is 2 cm thick. Find the value of the hundred-rupee notes that can be contained in a box of size 48 cm × 36 cm × 30 cm, if the bundles are tightly packed in it without any empty space.
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Volume of the box = 48 × 36 × 30 = 51840 cm³ Volume of 1 bundle = 15 × 8 × 2 = 240 cm³ Number of bundles = 51840 ÷ 240 = 216
Value per bundle = 125 × 100 = ₹12500
Total Value = 216 × 12500 = ₹27, 00, 000 = ₹27 Lakhs
∴ The correct answer is ₹27 Lakhs.

Alternate Method
Given:
Dimensions of a 100 - rupee note = 15 cm × 8 cm
Thickness of a bundle of 125 notes = 2 cm
Dimensions of the box = 48 cm × 36 cm × 30 cm

Formula Used:
Volume of a cuboid = Length × Breadth × Height
Number of items = Total Container Volume ÷ Volume of 1 item

Calculations:
⇒ Volume of the box = 48 × 36 × 30 = 51840 cm³ ⇒ Volume of 1 bundle = 15 × 8 × 2 = 240 cm³ ⇒ Number of bundles = 51840 ÷ 240 = 216
⇒ Total notes in the box = 216 × 125 = 27000 notes
⇒ Total value of the notes = 27000 × ₹100 = ₹27, 00, 000
⇒ Total value in Lakhs = ₹27 Lakhs
∴ The correct answer is ₹27 Lakhs.

Additional Information
Cuboid Volume

The space occupied by a 3 - dimensional solid with rectangular faces is its volume, calculated strictly as Length × Breadth × Height.

Packaging Optimization

When checking how many small items perfectly fit into a larger container without any gaps, divide the total volume of the container by the volume of a single small unit.

Number System Units

In the Indian numbering system, 1 Lakh equals 1, 00, 000 (one hundred thousand). This conversion simplifies managing large monetary values in competitive exams.

subject: Mathematics
questionText: The radius and height of a right circular cone are in the ratio $3 : 7$. If the volume of the cone is $528\text{ cm}^3$, then what is the height of the cone? $\left(\text{Take }\pi = \frac{22}{7}\right)$
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
For a right circular cone: $\text{Volume} = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$

Given ratio $r : h = 3 : 7$. Let $r = 3x$ and $h = 7x$: $\text{Volume} = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times (3x)^2 \times (7x)$

$\Rightarrow \text{Volume} = \frac{1}{3} \times 22 \times 9x^2 \times x = 66x^3$

We are given the volume as $528\text{ cm}^3$: $\Rightarrow 66x^3 = 528$

$\Rightarrow x^3 = \frac{528}{66} = 8$

$\Rightarrow x = \sqrt[3]{8} = 2$

Height of the cone: $\Rightarrow h = 7x = 7 \times 2 = 14\text{ cm}$
∴ The height of the cone is $14.0\text{ cm}$.

subject: Mathematics
questionText: The diameter of a metallic sphere is 6 cm. The sphere is melted and drawn into a wire of uniform circular cross-section. If the length of the wire is 36 m, then what is its radius equal to?
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Equate the volumes directly: Volume of Sphere = Volume of cylindrical Wire.
⇒ 4/3 × π × R³ = π × r² × h
⇒ 4/3 × 33 = r² × 3600 (Converting 36 m to 3600 cm)
⇒ 36 = r² × 3600
⇒ r² = 1/100 ⇒ r = 0.1 cm
∴ The correct answer is 0.1 cm.

Alternate Method
Given:
Diameter of the metallic sphere = 6 cm
Radius of the sphere (R) = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm
Length of the uniform wire (h) = 36 m
Converting length to cm ⇒ h = 36 × 100 = 3600 cm
Let the radius of the circular cross - section of the wire be r cm.

Formula Used:
Volume of a Sphere = 4/3 × π × R³ Volume of a Cylinder (Wire) = π × r² × h

Calculations:
When an object is melted and recast into another shape, the total volume remains conserved.

⇒ Volume of the cylindrical wire = Volume of the metallic sphere
⇒ π × r² × h = 4/3 × π × R³ ⇒ π × r² × 3600 = 4/3 × π × 33

Canceling π from both sides:

⇒ r² × 3600 = 4/3 × 27
⇒ r² × 3600 = 4 × 9
⇒ r² × 3600 = 36
⇒ r² = 36 ÷ 3600
⇒ r² = 1 / 100

Taking the square root on both sides:

⇒ r = √(1/100)
⇒ r = 1/10 = 0.1 cm
∴ The correct answer is 0.1 cm.

Additional Information
Principle of Recasting

When a 3D solid is melted and transformed into a completely different shape, its volume remains constant while the surface area may change.

Volume of a Sphere

The total 3D space occupied by a sphere of radius r is calculated using the standard formula V = 4/3 × π × r³.

Volume of a Cylinder

A circular wire is treated geometrically as a solid cylinder. Its volume is V = π × r² × h, where r is the radius of the circular base and h is the length or height of the wire.

subject: Mathematics
questionText: A cube of side 15 cm is cut into 27 small cubes. Then find the ratio of the lateral surface area of the large cube to the total surface area of one of the small cubes.
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Number of small cubes = (A/a)³ = 27 ⇒ Ratio of sides (A/a) = 3.
Ratio of areas = (Lateral Surface Area of Large Cube) ÷ (Total Surface Area of Small Cube)
⇒ (4 × A²) ÷ (6 × a²)
⇒ (4/6) × (A/a)² = (2/3) × 32 = 6
∴ The correct answer is 6 : 1.

Alternate Method
Given:
Side of the large cube (A) = 15 cm
Number of small cubes formed = 27

Formula Used:
Volume of cube = (side)³ Lateral Surface Area of cube = 4 × (side)² Total Surface Area of cube = 6 × (side)² Calculations:
⇒ Volume of large cube = 27 × Volume of small cube
⇒ 153 = 27 × a³ ⇒ 3375 = 27 × a³ ⇒ a³ = 125 ⇒ a = 5 cm
⇒ Lateral Surface Area of large cube = 4 × 152 = 4 × 225 = 900 cm² ⇒ Total Surface Area of small cube = 6 × 52 = 6 × 25 = 150 cm² ⇒ Required Ratio = 900 / 150 = 6 / 1 = 6 : 1
∴ The correct answer is 6 : 1.

Additional Information
Total Surface Area of a Cube

It is the sum of the areas of all 6 faces of the cube. Formula: TSA = 6 × (side)² Lateral Surface Area of a Cube

It is the sum of the areas of the 4 vertical side faces of the cube, excluding the top and bottom faces. Formula: LSA = 4 × (side)² Volume of a Cube

It represents the total 3D space occupied by the cube. When a shape is cut or reshaped, the total volume remains conserved. Formula: Volume = (side)³

subject: Mathematics
questionText: If the area of the base of a right circular cone is 157 cm² and its slant height is \sqrt{491} cm, then the volume of the cone is _______ (Use π = 3.14).
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Given Base Area = 157 cm², so π × r² = 157 ⇒ r² = 157 ÷ 3.14 = 50.
Height h = √(l² - r²) = √(491 - 50) = √441 = 21 cm.
Volume of cone = (1/3) × Base Area × Height.
Volume = (1/3) × 157 × 21 = 157 × 7 = 1099 cm³.
∴ The correct answer is 1099 cm³.

Alternate Method
Given:
Base area of the cone = 157 cm² Slant height (l) = √491 cm
(π = 3.14)

Formula Used:
Area of base = π × r² Calculations:
⇒ Area of base = π × r² = 157
⇒ 3.14 × r² = 157
⇒ r² = 157 ÷ 3.14 = 50
⇒ We know that, l² = r² + h² ⇒ (√491)2 = 50 + h² ⇒ 491 = 50 + h² ⇒ h² = 491 - 50 = 441
⇒ h = √441 = 21 cm
⇒ Volume of the cone = 1/3 × π × r² × h
⇒ Volume = 1/3 × (3.14 × 50) × 21
⇒ Volume = 1/3 × 157 × 21
⇒ Volume = 157 × 7 = 1099 cm³ ∴ The correct answer is 1099 cm³.

Additional Information
Volume of a Cone vs Cylinder

A cone's volume is exactly one - third of the volume of a cylinder with the same base radius and height. The formula is V = 1/3 × πr²h.

Surface Area of a Cone

The curved surface area is given by πrl and the total surface area is given by πr(r + l), where r is the radius and l is the slant height.

Frustum of a Cone

When a cone is sliced parallel to its base, the remaining lower part is called a frustum. Its volume is⅓ × πh(R² + r² + Rr).

subject: Mathematics
questionText: The radius of a cylinder is 5 cm more than its height. If the curved surface area of the cylinder is 792 cm², then the volume of the cylinder (in cm³), is ________. [Use \(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\) ]
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2 × π × r × h = 792 ⇒ π × r × h = 396
Volume of a cylinder is π × r² × h = (π × r × h) × r = 396 × Rs. ince 2 × (22/7) × r × (r - 5) = 792 ⇒ r × (r - 5) = 126
By simple observation, 14 × (14 - 5) = 126, so the radius r = 14 cm
Volume = 396 × 14 = 5544 cm³ ∴ The correct answer is 5544 cm³.

Alternate Method
Given:
Radius of cylinder (r) = height (h) + 5
Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 792 cm² Formula Used: Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2 × π × r × h
Volume of cylinder = π × r² × h

Calculation:
⇒ 2 × (22/7) × (h + 5) × h = 792
⇒ (44/7) × (h² + 5h) = 792
⇒ h² + 5h = 792 × 7 ÷ 44
⇒ h² + 5h = 18 × 7
⇒ h² + 5h - 126 = 0
⇒ h² + 14h - 9h - 126 = 0
⇒ h(h + 14) - 9(h + 14) = 0
⇒ (h - 9)(h + 14) = 0
⇒ h = 9 cm (since height cannot be negative)
⇒ Radius (r) = 9 + 5 = 14 cm
⇒ Volume = (22/7) × (14)² × 9
⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 196 × 9 = 22 × 28 × 9
⇒ Volume = 616 × 9 = 5544 cm³ ∴ The correct answer is 5544 cm³.

Additional Information
Properties of a Cylinder

A cylinder is a 3D solid with two parallel circular bases. Total Surface Area (TSA) = CSA + 2 × Base Area = 2 × π × r × (r + h).

Volume of Related Shapes

The volume of a cone with the same base radius and height as a cylinder is exactly one - third of the cylinder's volume. Cone Volume = (1/3) × π × r² × h.

Circumference and Area of Base

The base of a cylinder is a circle. Base Area = π × r² and Base Perimeter (Circumference) = 2 × π × r. The CSA can directly be calculated as Base Perimeter × height.

question: Three solid iron cubes of edges 8 cm, 10 cm and 12 cm are melted together to make a new cube. It is observed that 496 cm³ of the melted material is lost due to improper handling. The area (in cm²) of the whole surface of the newly formed cube is:
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total volume of given cubes = 83 + 103 + 123 = 512 + 1000 + 1728 = 3240 cm³ Volume of the new cube = 3240 - 496 = 2744 cm³ Side of the new cube (a) = 3√2744 = 14 cm
Total Surface Area = 6a² = 6 × 142 = 6 × 196 = 1176 cm² ∴ The correct answer is 1176 cm².

Alternate Method
Given:
Edges of the three solid iron cubes = 8 cm, 10 cm, and 12 cm
Melted material lost due to improper handling = 496 cm³ Formula Used: Volume of a cube = a³ Total surface area of a cube = 6a² Calculations:
⇒ Total volume of the three smaller cubes = (83 + 103 + 123) cm³ ⇒ Total volume = 512 + 1000 + 1728 = 3240 cm³ ⇒ Volume of the newly formed cube = Total Initial Volume - Material Lost
⇒ Volume of the new cube = 3240 - 496 = 2744 cm³ ⇒ Let the edge length of the new cube be 'a' cm.
⇒ a³ = 2744
⇒ a = 3√2744 = 14 cm
⇒ Area of the whole surface of the new cube = 6a² ⇒ Surface Area = 6 × (14)² ⇒ Surface Area = 6 × 196 = 1176 cm² ∴ The correct answer is 1176 cm².

Additional Information
Total Surface Area of a Cube

The total surface area of a cube is the combined area of its 6 identical square faces. Formula: TSA = 6a².

Lateral Surface Area of a Cube

The lateral surface area includes only the 4 vertical faces, excluding the top and bottom faces. Formula: LSA = 4a².

Volume of a Cube

The volume of a cube represents the 3D space occupied by it. Formula: Volume = a³.

Diagonal of a Cube

The length of the longest line segment connecting two opposite interior corners of a cube. Formula: Diagonal = a√3.
